findings.location: source.html — Ecclesiastes quotation and Deuteronomy/Galatians inline quotations
findings.source_quote:
Ecclesiastes 12:1-7 gives a somewhat dismal view of the aging process. “Remember now thy Creator in the days of thy youth, ... Then shall the dust return to the earth as it was: and the spirit shall return unto God who gave it.”

...

“And thou shalt teach them diligently unto thy children, and shalt talk of them when thou sittest in thine house, and when thou walkest by the way, and when thou liest down, and when thou risest up” (Deuteronomy 6:7).

...

“But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, longsuffering, gentleness, goodness, faith, meekness, temperance: against such there is no law” (Galatians 5:22-23).
findings.suggested_fix:
The long quoted biblical passage and the two shorter verse quotations appear in the source as English. In the Spanish translation they must convey the printed English wording (i.e., translate the printed English phrases into Spanish while preserving theological meaning and the author’s quoted wording). Replace the English quotation text with an accurate Spanish rendering of the quoted English text, keeping the same punctuation and quotation-mark placement and leaving the verse references as in the source. Example (one possible rendering that keeps the sense of the printed English):
- Replace the Ecclesiastes block with a Spanish translation that follows the printed English lines, e.g. “Acuérdate ahora de tu Creador en los días de tu juventud, antes que vengan los días malos, y lleguen los años de los cuales digas: No tengo en ellos contentamiento; … Entonces volverá el polvo a la tierra, como era, y el espíritu volverá a Dios que lo dio.”
- Replace the Deuteronomy and Galatians quoted lines with Spanish translations conveying the printed English wording (keeping the verse references unchanged).
Preserve the exact HTML tags (paragraph and citation structure) and do not substitute a different Bible version text that changes wording or theology.
